## Communications Framework for Faith‑Based & Cultural Seasonal Campaigns **Goal:** Create season‑specific messages (Ramadan, Lunar New Year, Diwali …) that feel authentic in every market, pass a rigorous multi‑layered approval process, and can be monitored, defended or corrected in real‑time when social‑media scrutiny spikes. --- ### 1. Strategic Foundations | Pillar | What it Guarantees | How to Embed | |--------|-------------------|--------------| | **Purpose‑First** | Campaigns start from a clear social‑good or brand‑value intention (e.g., “share‑the‑blessing,” “celebrate togetherness”) rather than a sales‑first hook. | Draft a **Seasonal Purpose Statement** (≤ 1 sentence) for each holiday and lock it into the brief. | | **Cultural‑Integrity Charter** | A written commitment that the brand will only use symbols, language and practices that are **accurate, respectful, and co‑created** with local cultural custodians. | Sign‑off by the **Global Cultural Advisory Board (GCAB)** and keep the charter on the internal intranet as a “non‑negotiable.” | | **One‑Core‑Engine, Multi‑Tenant Design** | Central creative kernel (tone, visual style, brand DNA) can be *re‑used* but each market gets its own **local “tenant” layer** (language, motifs, religious nuance). | Adopt a **“core‑plus‑local” asset matrix** (see Section 3). | | **Transparency & Dialogue** | Audiences see the brand **listening** and **responding** quickly, reducing backlash momentum. | Build a **Real‑Time Engagement Hub (RTEH)** for social‑listening, briefing, and rapid response. | --- ### 2. Governance & Approval Safeguards #### 2.1 Organisational Structure ``` Global Cultural Advisory Board (GCAB) ├─ Global Head of Cultural Insight ├─ Chief Marketing Officer (CMO) └─ External Scholars & NGOs (rotating) ┌───────────────────────┐ │ Regional Cultural Council (RCC) – 4 x (Gulf‑NA, MENA‑NA, SE‑Asia, APAC‑Other) │ └───────────────────────┘ │ ┌──────────┴───────────┐ │ │ Creative Agency Local Insight Partner (global‑lead) (national NGOs, religious scholars, community leaders, market‑research firm) ``` * **GCAB** – approves **global purpose, brand tone, and universal visual assets** (e.g., brand colour palette, logo usage). * **RCC** – reviews **regional adaptations**, validates religious accuracy, signs‑off on **local copy, imagery, audio**. * **Local Insight Partner** – provides **on‑the‑ground vetting** (e.g., a Saudi‑based Islamic‑studies department, a Tamil‑cultural NGO in Singapore). #### 2.2 Approval Flow (Step‑by‑Step) | Step | Who | Deliverable | “Gate” Criteria (✓/✗) | |------|-----|-------------|------------------------| | 1️⃣ Brief & Purpose | Global Brand Lead → GCAB | **Seasonal Purpose Statement** + high‑level *must‑have* cultural elements | Purpose aligns with brand values & is *not* commercial‑only | | 2️⃣ Research Pack | Global Insight Lead → RCC + Local Partner | Ethnographic diary, consumer sentiment map, taboo list, key rituals | ✅ All “taboo” items flagged; ✅‑verified source citations | | 3️⃣ Core Creative Concept | Global Agency (lead) → GCAB | Core visual & audio engine (brand‑centric) | ✅ Brand‑consistent, no cultural symbols yet | | 4️⃣ Local Adaptation Brief | RCC → Local Agency/Partner | Spec for language, symbols, local customs, imagery | ✅ All local symbols sourced from approved libraries | | 5️⃣ Creative Production | Local Agency + Global Agency (co‑edit) | Mock‑ups, copy, video scripts, AR/VR assets | ✗ Any element breaching **taboo list** → sent back | | 6️⃣ First‑Round Review | Local Insight Partner → RCC | **Cultural Accuracy Checklist** (see Annex A) | ✅ All checks pass | | 7️⃣ Legal & Regulatory Check | Global Legal + Local Legal | Compliance with advertising, food‑labeling, religious‑sensitivity law | ✅ No breach of local regulations (e.g., Saudi “Halal Advertising Code”) | | 8️⃣ Final Sign‑off | **GCAB + RCC** (joint approval) | **Go‑Live Package** (assets + approval matrix) | ✅ All gates cleared | | 9️⃣ Pre‑Launch Social‑Listening Test | RTEH (24 h simulated monitoring) | Early‑alert risk score (< 3 / 10) | ✗ If risk > 3 → re‑review | | 🔟 Launch & Live‑Monitoring | RTEH → Social‑Media Ops | Real‑time dashboard (sentiment, spikes, volume) | Continuous | *The **“Gate”** is a binary pass/fail; any “✗” sends the asset back to the previous step with a mandatory **“Remediation Note.”** --- ### 3. Creative Architecture – “Core + Local” Asset Matrix | Asset Type | Core (Global) | Local “Tenant” Layer | Example (Ramadan) | |------------|---------------|----------------------|-------------------| | **Visual Palette** | Brand primary colours, logo placements, 3‑second animation template | Accent colour(s) tied to local tradition (e.g., green & gold for Gulf, deep orange for Indonesia, indigo for Morocco) | Core logo + Crescent; local background lantern style | | **Tagline** | Short, brand‑centric (< 6 words) | Translated + culturally‑tuned, **no literal back‑translation** | Global: “Together, we share.”
Gulf: “نشارك الخير معاً” (Nasharik Al‑Khair Ma’an) | | **Audio** | Signature jingle (instrumental) | Instrumentation & language (e.g., *oud* for Gulf, *gamelan* for Indonesia, *bansuri* for India) | 30‑sec video: Global melody + local violin/oud overlay | | **Iconography** | Brand‑approved icons (e.g., hand‑offering, plate) | Symbolic motifs vetted by local scholars (e.g., *hanbokr* for Ramadan, *灯笼* for Lunar New Year) | Core plate → add *pharaonic* pattern for North‑Africa | | **Storyline** | Narrative arc: “pre‑fast → iftar → sharing” (global) | Insert local rituals (e.g., *Suhoor* in Malaysia, *Taraweeh* in Saudi, *Buka Puasa* in Indonesia) | Video: same structure, but each market shows its own family gathering scene | | **Digital Activations** | Hashtag framework (#ShareTheBlessing) | Regional hashtag + emoji (e.g., #RamadanKareem🕌 vs #RamadanKareem🕌🇸🇦) | Co‑branded AR filter: Global logo + local lantern style | **Key Rule:** **No local asset may be released without a GCAB‑signed “Cultural‑Fit Certificate”** (downloadable PDF attached to each asset). --- ### 4. Research & Insight Pipeline (Authenticity Engine) 1. **Desk Scan (6 months before)** – Pull in academic research, media coverage, government guidelines (e.g., Saudi Ministry of Islamic Affairs Ramadan media code). 2. **Community‑Co‑Creation Workshops** – 3‑hour virtual sessions with **10–12 community leaders** (imams, Hindu priests, Chinese New‑Year elders, etc.) to surface *must‑include* and *must‑avoid* elements. 3. **Micro‑Testing (A/B) on “Trusted Panels”** – Run quick video or copy tests on **closed‑group platforms** (e.g., WhatsApp groups in Indonesia, Facebook “Moms of Morocco”) to gauge perceived authenticity (Likert 1‑5). 4. **Bias & Sensitivity Scan** – Run all copy & imagery through an **AI‑enhanced bias detector** trained on a curated corpus of culturally tagged content. Flag any term > 0.8 probability of being “potentially offensive.” **Deliverable:** **Cultural Insight Dossier** (PDF) + **Authenticity Scorecard** (0‑10). Score ≥ 8 required for GCAB sign‑off. --- ### 5. Real‑Time Scrutiny Management | Component | Tool/Process | Owner | Frequency | |-----------|--------------|-------|-----------| | **Social‑Listening Dashboard** | Sprinklr + Meltwater + custom NLP sentiment model (Arabic, Bahasa, Tamil, Mandarin, Hindi) | RTEH Lead | 24/7, alerts on ± 20 % sentiment swing | | **Early‑Warning “Risk Radar”** | Auto‑generated heat‑map (topics, volume, sentiment, influencer amplification) | RTEH Analyst | Immediate on‑launch, then every 2 h | | **Response Playbook** | Tier‑1 (thanks/clarify), Tier‑2 (public apology + corrective post), Tier‑3 (legal escalation) | Social‑Media Ops + Crisis Manager | Triggered by risk score > 5 | | **Influencer Amplification Buffer** | Pre‑approved “cultural champion” accounts ready to post supportive content within 30 min of launch. | Regional Agency | On‑call schedule | | **Cross‑Border Notification Loop** | Automated email to **all RCCs** when any market’s risk score passes threshold; simultaneous translation of key posts. | RTEH System | Real‑time | **Example Scenario – Ramadan in Gulf:** - At T+0: Campaign goes live. - At T+30 min: Sentiment drops 22 % in Saudi after a tweet cites “dates” as “sweet fruit of the desert” (perceived as a stereotype). - RTEH flags **Risk = 6** → Tier‑2 playbook → Immediate **regional apology video** featuring a Saudi‑based brand ambassador, plus an updated copy version. - Simultaneously, **GCAB** sends a brief internal note confirming the correction aligns with the **Cultural‑Fit Certificate**. --- ### 6. Crisis Management Protocol | Phase | Action | Owner | Timeline | |------|--------|-------|----------| | **Detection** | Social‑listening alert → verify authenticity (human check) | RTEH Analyst | ≤ 15 min | | **Assessment** | Classify severity (Low/Medium/High) using **Impact‑Likelihood Matrix** (see Annex B) | Crisis Manager | ≤ 30 min | | **Decision** | Approve response tier (quick thank‑you, clarification, apology) | RCC Lead + GCAB (if High) | ≤ 45 min | | **Response** | Draft, translate, and post response; engage influencer buffer | Social‑Media Ops + Local Agency | ≤ 90 min | | **Escalation** | If legal or regulatory breach suspected → involve Global Legal, local counsel | Crisis Manager | Immediate | | **Post‑Mortem** | Capture metrics, update **Cultural‑Fit Checklist**, add learnings to “Lesson‑Bank.” | RTEH Lead | Within 48 h + full report 7 days | All statements must reference the **Cultural Integrity Charter** (“We respect the traditions of ___ and are listening to your feedback”) to reinforce goodwill. --- ### 7. Metrics & Learning Loop | KPI | Target (per season) | Measurement Tool | |-----|--------------------|------------------| | **Authenticity Score** (pre‑launch) | ≥ 8 /10 | Insight Dossier scorecard | | **Sentiment Lift** (first 48 h) | +10 pts vs. baseline | Sprinklr sentiment index | | **Engagement Rate** (UGC shares) | ≥ 3 % of impressions | Platform analytics | | **Issue Rate** (negative spikes) | ≤ 2 % of total mentions | RTEH alerts | | **Resolution Time** (first corrective post) | ≤ 90 min for Medium‑High risk | Crisis log | | **Brand‑Trust Lift** (post‑campaign survey) | +5 pts NPS | Online panel | | **Compliance Pass** (legal & Sharia) | 100 % | Legal sign‑off audit | Every season ends with a **“Cultural Playbook Update”** that feeds back into **Annex A (Checklist)** and **ANNEX B (Risk Matrix)**. --- ### 8. Annex A – Cultural Accuracy Checklist (mandatory for every asset) | Item | Question | Evidence Required | |------|----------|-------------------| | **Religious Symbol Use** | Is the symbol (crescent, diya, lotus) *officially permitted* in commercial settings in this market? | Photo of local authority guideline OR written approval from a recognized religious council | | **Language Nuance** | Does the copy avoid literal translations that change meaning (e.g., “Ramadan Kareem” vs. “Ramadan Mubarak”)? | Linguistic review sign‑off from a certified translator | | **Ritual Timing** | Does the story timeline respect local practice (e.g., Suhoor before dawn, Diwali “Lakshmi Puja” on day 1)? | Calendar reference + verification note from community workshop | | **Food‑Halal/Kosher/Vegetarian Rules** | Are all displayed foods compliant with the holiday’s dietary law? | Ingredient list + certification (Halal cert. number, etc.) | | **Visual Representation** | Do the models reflect the demographic diversity of the market (age, gender, dress code)? | Photo‑release forms + demographic audit sheet | | **Color & Pattern Sensitivity** | Are colours/patterns historically or politically charged? (e.g., red in some Gulf contexts can connote danger) | Color‑cultural matrix signed by local partner | | **Music & Audio** | Is any background music permissible (e.g., devotional chants vs. pop beats) for the occasion? | Audio‑rights clearance + cultural advisor note | | **Social Norms** | Does any scene imply prohibited behavior (e.g., public drinking during Ramadan, “gift‑giving” that could be seen as bribery)? | Scene‑by‑scene risk rating (Low/Medium/High) | All rows **must be ticked “Yes”** before the **Cultural‑Fit Certificate** is issued. --- ### 9. Annex B – Impact‑Likelihood Risk Matrix | Impact \ Likelihood | **Rare (<5 %)** | **Possible (5‑20 %)** | **Likely (>20 %)** | |--------------------|----------------|----------------------|--------------------| | **Catastrophic** (brand‑wide boycott, regulator fine) | **Red –** monitor only | **Red –** immediate escalation to GCAB + legal | **Red –** suspend all related assets, issue public apology | | **Major** (viral criticism, media coverage) | **Orange –** prepare response | **Orange –** post clarification within 2 h | **Orange –** issue correction + influencer amplification | | **Moderate** (negative comments, low‑volume backlash) | **Yellow –** note for future learnings | **Yellow –** respond within 24 h, monitor | **Yellow –** respond, adjust assets for next market | | **Minor** (neutral chatter) | **Green –** no action needed | **Green –** monitor | **Green –** track for trend analysis | **Risk Rating** = Impact × Likelihood (scale 1‑9). Any rating **≥ 5** triggers the **Crisis Management Protocol**. --- ### 10. Implementation Timeline (12‑Month Cycle) | Month | Milestone | |-------|-----------| | **0‑1** | Assemble **GCAB** and **RCCs**; sign **Cultural Integrity Charter** | | **1‑2** | Commission **Cultural Insight Dossiers** for Ramadan, Lunar New Year, Diwali | | **2‑3** | Core creative concept workshop (global agency) | | **3‑4** | Local adaptation briefs issued; local partners onboard | | **4‑5** | First‑round asset production & **Cultural Accuracy Checklist** completion | | **5‑6** | Legal & Sharia compliance review; generate **Cultural‑Fit Certificates** | | **6** | **Pre‑Launch Social‑Listening Test** (sandbox) | | **6‑7** | Final joint sign‑off (GCAB + RCC) → build **Go‑Live Package** | | **7** | Launch in **pilot market** (e.g., UAE for Ramadan, Singapore for Lunar New Year) | | **7‑8** | Real‑time monitoring; capture early‑alert data | | **8‑9** | Full rollout to remaining markets; apply learnings from pilot | | **9‑10** | Post‑campaign survey & brand‑trust audit | | **10‑12** | **Playbook Refresh** – update checklists, add new cultural partners, embed new AI‑bias model | --- ## QUICK‑START CHECKLIST (What the Brand Must Do Before the First Seasonal Campaign) | ✔️ | Action | |----|--------| | 1 | **Form GCAB** (include at least one AAOIFI‑qualified scholar, one local religious leader from each region, and a senior brand executive). | | 2 | Draft & circulate the **Cultural Integrity Charter** → get executive sign‑off. | | 3 | Sign contracts with **four local Insight Partners** (one per regional cluster) that commit to *co‑creation* and provide a **written cultural‑fit endorsement**. | | 4 | Deploy a **global NLP‑bias detector** trained on Arabic, Bahasa, Tamil, Mandarin, Hindi corpora; integrate into the creative review workflow. | | 5 | Build the **Real‑Time Engagement Hub** (dashboard + alert system) and train the social‑media ops team on the **Tiered Response Playbook**. | | 6 | Create the **Authenticity Scorecard template** and run a **pilot test** on a past campaign that received criticism; verify the score is ≥ 8 after remediation. | | 7 | Publish the **Cultural Accuracy Checklist** on the internal file server; make it a required field in the project‑management tool (e.g., Asana). | | 8 | Conduct a **cross‑border “War‑Room” mock drill** (simulate a backlash on a Ramadan post) to test the crisis‑response timeline. | | 9 | Release **pre‑approved “culture‑champion” influencer contracts** (incl. rapid‑response clause). | | 10| Set up **monthly reporting** to the Board on cultural‑risk metrics and lessons learned. | --- ### TL;DR - **One core brand engine** + **regional “tenant” layers** keep creative efficiency while allowing cultural specificity. - **Multi‑level governance** (GCAB → RCC → local partners) forces real‑time, on‑the‑ground validation before any public release. - **Mandatory checklists, AI‑bias scans, and a pre‑launch “Risk Radar”** catch mis‑representations *before* they go live. - **Real‑Time Engagement Hub + Tiered Playbook** give the brand the speed to reply within minutes, turning potential backlash into an opportunity to show listening. - **Post‑campaign learning loop** updates the Cultural Playbook, ensuring each season becomes a higher‑authenticity benchmark. By institutionalising this framework, the global food brand can run Ramadan, Lunar New Year, Diwali and other faith‑based campaigns **with confidence that the message is locally genuine, regulator‑approved, and ready to be defended instantly when the digital spotlight turns**.
